'''Dooku's palace''' was located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]] and was the home of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the palace was protected by [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].

==Exterior==
[[File:Dooku_palace_by_night.png|thumb|left|250px|The front side of the palace by night]]
The palace of [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] stood on its own grounds, a rectangular area located on a cliff face. Upon arrival, visitors would take the long, paved walkway that led to the keep and was flanked at either side by three ornamental gardens.<ref name="TCW312" /> In front of the palace's main entrance was a double line of obelisks.<ref name="TCW314">{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}}</ref> The main tower, in which the Count's quarters were contained, was as high as near 119 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]. It also featured a grand, 22-meter high<ref name="BoxConc">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-box-concept-art-gallery|text="The Box" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|slide 4}}</ref><ref name="Height">According to ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'', the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] all measured 1.83 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]. The height of the tower can be obtained by multiplying that of a standard clone trooper by 65, which gives 118.95 meters. The castle's [[Glass|StainGlass]] [[Window/Legends|window]] is also shown to be twelve times higher than a clone trooper, which gives 21.96 meters.</ref> stained glass [[Window/Legends|window]] on cliff side.<ref name="BoxConc" /> What appeared to be ten secondary buildings scattered on the palace's grounds<ref name="TCW312" /> were in fact a network of [[relay tower]]s with incandescent windows.<ref name="BoxConc" />

==Interior==
Dooku's palace was lavishly decorated with many statues and elaborate paintings. His private quarters were made up of luxurious furnishings. The palace also had various [[Droid/Legends|droids]] to tend to the Count and his guests.

==History==
When [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] turned his back on the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]<ref>{{Film|II}}</ref> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref>[[The New Essential Chronology|''The New Essential Chronology'']]</ref> he reclaimed his title, wealth and territory, moving his base of operations to a cliff-side palace with a commanding view of the lush [[Forest/Legends|forests]] of his homeworld.<ref>{{SWE|locations|serenno|Serenno}}</ref>

In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Legends-Date">{{TCWdates|312}}</ref> [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], along with two [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], launched an assassination attempt on the Count while he was sleeping. However, it failed and the palace sustained damage in the process.<ref name="TCW312" /> [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] then brought [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] to the palace to become Dooku's new [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Acolyte]]. Dooku then tested Savage by sending him to [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]] to capture a key military base. Savage then successfully returned to Dooku to be trained to become his new Dark Acolyte.<ref name="Monster">{{TCW|Monster}}</ref> He taught Savage that his anger gave him strength and that he must feed off it to succeed. He then sent him on a mission to [[Toydaria/Legends|Toydaria]] to capture [[King/Legends|King]] [[Katuunko/Legends|Katuunko]].<ref name="TCW314" />

[[File:DookuThroneRoom-Massacre.png|thumb|right|250px|The throne room of Dooku's palace]]
Later on, mastermind [[Moralo Eval/Legends|Moralo Eval]] constructed the [[Box/Legends|Box]] outside of the palace for training [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], in order to kidnap [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="The Box">{{TCW|The Box}}</ref>

Later Dooku summoned [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] to [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]] and ordered him to kill Ventress and the Nightsisters on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. Mother Talzin attempted to kill Dooku while he was in his base, which caused him terrible agony, but he contacted Grievous via comlink and ordered that he kill Talzin and follow the green mist which would take him to her. Dooku was saved by Grievous at the last moment.<ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref> He then believed that the Nightsisters were destroyed so he redirected his attention to Savage Opress, his former apprentice. He summoned Grievous to his base and told him that he could sense that Opress was growing stronger each day. Although Grievous dismissed the fact that Savage could be considered a threat, Dooku said he was a threat to all people including themselves and that something sinister was rising.<ref name="Brothers">{{TCW|Brothers (episode)}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Dooku's palace made its first appeared in "[[Nightsisters (episode)|Nightsisters]]", the twelfth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']] television series which aired on [[January 7]], [[2011]].<ref name="TCW312"/> It was identified as a palace in the Concept Art Gallery on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="BoxConc" />

In the current [[canon]], the palace is named [[Castle Serenno]].<ref name="DJL">''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]''</ref>
